prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

U0022: As of 2023, all aspects of space missions have been monitored and coordinated with reliance on Earth-based Mission Control Center (MCC).
U0023: However, anticipated delays in radio communications and blackouts require future missions to be independent from Earth in a way not yet seen in space flight.
U0024: Crew on these long duration missions will need technologies that promote autonomy across all phases of flight.
U0025: Objective OP-2 from the architecture document reads Optimize operations, training and interaction between the team on Earth, crew members on orbit, and a Martian surface team considering communication delays, autonomy level, and time required for an early return to the Earth.
U0026: In other words, technologies and new ways of working need to be developed to ensure mission goals are accomplished within the environmental constraints that will be present in future missions (e.g. limited communication bandwidth between all members of the flight team).
U0027: Imagining how to support all phases of a future mission in new ways, with novel technology is no easy feat.
U0028: This challenge broadly aligns with the envisioned world problem [16, 8] and is an active area of study within the fields of human factors and cognitive systems engineering [4, 3, 12].
U0029: For the purposes of this document, a subset of human spaceflight operations, known as EVA [7, 15, 9], is offered as a case study for how to begin the process of enabling Earth-independence.
U0030: The methods employed in this document are inspired by the deliberate discussion of user context [14, 13, 1], function allocation [2], and work domain construction [8].
U0031: Collectively, these approaches attempt to help imagine the work domain that might one day exist and grapple with the practical realities of working in that hypothetical future.
U0032: Revision: Rev A Document No: CTSD-ADV-1788 Effective Date: November, 2023 Page: Page 14 of 110 Title: Concept of Operations 3 Advanced Informatics Display System and EVA Concept of Operations Definition The contents of this document aim to explore hypothetical future moments during EVA execution to establish more specific account of the contextually relevant details of existing concept of operations documents.
U0033: Specifically, Section 5 explores moments within Phase 7 "EVA Operations" as shown in Figure 3.1.
U0034: Section 6 describes potential solutions within the context of those hypothesized moments to help show how a spacesuit-compatible informatics system could help the user in that particular situation.
U0035: Section 4 provides an overview of the methods involved in this detailed concept of operations process.
U0036: The remainder of this section describes how this document builds upon details found in parent concept of operations documents (Section 3.1).
U0037: Additionally, Section 3.2 provides rationale on why a spacesuit-compatible augmented reality informatics system is the highest value proposition solution regarding an EVA informatics display system. 3.1 Con-Ops Traceability Below is a list of the governing documents that were used to prioritize the scope of content in this document. • EVA-EXP-0042 - Exploration EVA System Concept of Operations • xEVAS System Requirement Document, specifically RQMT-065 Figure 3.1 outlines the over-arching phases of operation that are anticipated to be involved in future EVA operations.
U0038: Section 7.2.8 and APPENDIX F of EVA-EXP-0042 also adds details regarding the variety of potential engineering and science tasks crew might perform.
U0039: APPENDIX H INFORMAT- ICS outlines a list of potentially desirable advanced digital content capabilities.
U0040: The exploration EVA system found in EVA-EXP-0042 is shown in Figure 3.2 with annotations of the anticipated interconnections that will be required if an advanced informatics display such as an augmented reality display is to ever be realized [10].
U0041: A central point of this annotated diagram is that an advanced informatics device must not only service the needs of the suited crew member, but it must also support the broader team of remote support personnel and accommodate interfaces with a variety of other EVA assets.
U0042: In other words, the advanced informatics device cannot simply be designed for a single user when EVA operations requires a team of people and a variety of assets.
U0043: Most recently, the xEVAS System Requirements Document (SRD) outlines the expected advanced informatics capabilities of future spacesuits within RQMT-065.
U0044: This content is summarized along- side the desired features outlined in EVA-EXP-0042 in Figure 3.3 to help bound the capabilities discussed in the remainder of this document.
U0045: Seven of the ten requirement statements align with concept of operations expectations.
